Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. messages.content:
The `appendFixedWidthPadRight` method in the `StrBuilder` class handles appending a given object with a fixed width and padding on the right. The method checks if the width is greater than 0, ensures the capacity of the buffer, converts the object to a string (handling null case), and then appends the string with padding on the right.

Looking at the failing test case, `testLang412Right`, it initializes a `StrBuilder` instance and then calls `appendFixedWidthPadRight` with a `null` object, a width of 10, and a padding character of '*'.

The current bug report mentions that appending a null value with fixed width causes a null pointer exception if `getNullText()` has not been set. In the `appendFixedWidthPadRight` method, it handles the null case by converting the object to a string using `obj.toString()`. If `obj` is null and `getNullText()` has not been set, then calling `obj.toString()` could lead to a `NullPointerException`.

To resolve this issue, the method should have additional null checking for `obj` before calling `obj.toString()` to prevent a `NullPointerException` when `obj` is null.

Next, I will provide the best location to fix this issue.
```
org.apache.commons.lang.text.StrBuilder.appendFixedWidthPadRight(java.lang.Object, int, char)
```
